strings.name: Ichiro Suzuki
strings.summary: Suzuki trained in Japanese high-school baseball and joined Orix in 1992, becoming a leading NPB player through contact hitting, speed and defense. He joined Seattle in 2001, winning both American League Rookie of the Year and MVP, and recorded 262 hits in 2004. He also helped Japan win the World Baseball Classic and, after retiring, entered the US National Baseball Hall of Fame in 2025.

strings.highlights.h1.title: Hitting across Japan and America
strings.highlights.h1.text: Built hitting achievements in NPB and MLB alongside baserunning and outfield defense.
strings.highlights.h2.title: US Baseball Hall of Fame
strings.highlights.h2.text: In 2025 became the first Japanese player elected to the US National Baseball Hall of Fame.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Enters Hall of Fame
strings.timeline.t1.text: Joined the US National Baseball Hall of Fame’s class of 2025 in recognition of his career.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Playing career ends in Tokyo
strings.timeline.t2.text: Retired after appearing for Seattle in the Tokyo opening series, ending his long playing career.
strings.timeline.t3.title: 3,000 MLB hits
strings.timeline.t3.text: Reached 3,000 career MLB hits with a triple while playing for the Miami Marlins.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Another Classic title
strings.timeline.t4.text: Helped Japan win the World Baseball Classic again, delivering a crucial extra-inning hit in the final.
strings.timeline.t5.title: 262 hits in one season
strings.timeline.t5.text: Recorded 262 hits for Seattle, setting the MLB single-season hits record.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Awards in MLB debut season
strings.timeline.t6.text: Joined Seattle and won American League Rookie of the Year and Most Valuable Player.
strings.timeline.t7.title: NPB breakthrough
strings.timeline.t7.text: Became a regular Orix starter, winning the batting title and Pacific League MVP.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Professional career begins
strings.timeline.t8.text: Joined the Orix BlueWave after high school, beginning his professional career in Japan.
